patterns.usage_note: States a settled intention: 〜つもりだ reports a plan the speaker has already formed and holds (京都へ引っ越すつもりです). That pre-formed quality is what separates it from the on-the-spot 〜(よ)う, and it is why 何をするつもりですか put to a superior can sound accusatory. つもり is a noun, so it takes the dictionary form plus a copula; 〜ないつもりだ says the plan is not to act, while 〜つもりはない denies having any intention at all.

examples.ruby: 来月[らいげつ]、京都[きょうと]へ引[ひ]っ越[こ]すつもりです。
examples.english: I'm planning to move to Kyoto next month.

examples.ruby: この話[はなし]はまだ誰[だれ]にも伝[つた]えるつもりはない。
examples.english: I have no intention of passing this on to anyone yet.

examples.ruby: 今日[きょう]こそ早[はや]く寝[ね]るつもりだったのに、また夜更[よふ]かしした。
examples.english: Tonight of all nights I meant to get to bed early, and I stayed up late again.
